what: A predicted multimer with its predicted aligned error: human TNF-alpha as a homotrimer, three chains predicted together.
kept_how: In the repository: a prediction can be fetched from no archive. Two of its five draws are here, and the confidence summary of all five. The checksums are in this file.
terms: Predicted by the author of bindview; no third party's data. The files are part of this repository, under its licence.

cases.name: hTNFA_canonical_trimer
cases.molecule: human TNF-alpha, the soluble form, as a homotrimer: chains A, B and C, the same 157 residues in each, numbered 1 to 157
cases.sequence_from: the residues of chain A in the model files; chains B and C have the same. The sha256 is of the one-letter string above.
cases.made_with: Boltz: five diffusion samples (draws) of one prediction, ranked by the model's own confidence score, model_0 first. The files are in Boltz's output layout and name neither the program nor its version. The settings of the run were not recorded and sampling is random: a new run gives another prediction, not these files.
cases.in_repository: Draws 0 and 1 whole (model file, PAE matrix, pLDDT array, confidence summary) and the confidence summary of draws 2, 3 and 4: 11 files, 2218086 bytes.
cases.why_two_draws: A PAE matrix is 0.79 MB and does not compress. Draws 0 and 1 are the pair in which the three chains are named in another order, which reading several draws has to get right.

facts.row_order: plddt_*.npz times 100 equals the per-residue B-factor of the model file in file order to 0.0005, in both draws
facts.chain_names_across_draws: model_1 names the chains in the opposite order round the axis: CA RMSD on model_0 21.89 as named, 0.98 with B and C exchanged
